name: cloud.ferrite/ferrite
title: Ferrite
description: Build, deploy and run full-stack web apps from the conversation.

tools.name: validate_spec
tools.description: The spec in deploy_source's description passes as given with your names; run this only if you change more. Validate an InfraSpec (JSON) against the LIVE AICC admission gate (a spec that passes here passes at deploy). Returns {passed, violations:[{code,message,fix_it}], rejection_reasons}.

tools.name: code_gate
tools.description:
Check source policy before submission (no #![forbid(unsafe_code)] at the crate root = CODE_UNSAFE_PERMITTED; a dependency besides ferrite-app). Fix violations before continuing. Admission is not compilation or a test verdict. For existing-app repairs, commit changed files and deploy the exact returned reference; see rcs_commit.
Cargo.toml: [package] name="<name>" version="0.1.0" edition="2021" [dependencies] ferrite-app={path="../ferrite-app"}
API for handle() in deploy_source's loop. Request: req.method, req.path (may end ?query), req.body (Vec<u8>; a form post is urlencoded), req.idempotency_key, req.headers (only those the route lists, e.g. add "forward_headers":["cookie"] to the spec's route to read a cookie). Reply: let mut r=IngressReply::to(req,200,html.into_bytes()); r.headers.push(("content-type".into(),"text/html; charset=utf-8".into())); a form POST answers 303 with ("location","/"); at most one ("set-cookie",...) per reply. Store db, each call async -> io::Result: get(&[u8])->Option<Vec<u8>>; put(&[u8],&[u8]); add(&[u8],i64)->(new,version), an atomic counter get reads as decimal text; scan_prefix(prefix,None,500)->(Vec<(key,value,version)>,more); put_if_version(k,v,None).await?.is_ok() creates k only if absent. std and ferrite_app only (ferrite_app::serde_json), escape visitor text in HTML. #[test]s go in src/main.rs under #[cfg(test)]; deploy_source does not run them (see test_ref).
Returns {admitted, violations:[{code,detail}], test_admitted, test_violations, tests_scanned}. `packages` adds Ferrite source packages under src/<root>/.

files.description: map of relative path -> file content, e.g. {"Cargo.toml": "...", "src/lib.rs": "..."}

packages.description: Ferrite source packages to compile in, by name from list_packages ("name" or "name@version"). The server adds each package's files, and its dependencies', under src/<root>/ before anything reads `files`; declare each root in src/lib.rs (read_package gives the lines). Do not send those files yourself: a changed copy is refused.

tools.name: explain_gate
tools.description: Explain a gate violation code (CODE_*/APP_*/CAP_*/DELTA_*/SERVICE_*/SPEC_*/COMPUTE_*) and how to fix it. For spec violations, validate_spec's live fix_it is canonical.

tools.name: read_docs
tools.description: A small web app (poll, RSVP, sign-up sheet): read {"doc":"page-app-starter"}, a verified one-file app, and nothing else before the first deploy. Read further docs only when one specific API, gate code or bound blocks you. READ the Ferrite documentation. With no arguments: the agent brief (the rules to know before building) and the index of every document with its size. {"doc":"<id>"} returns a document of 12 KB or less whole and a larger one as its outline of section ids; then {"doc":"<id>","section":"<section id>"} returns one section, and {"doc":"<id>","full":true} returns everything. search_docs finds the right section fastest. The same documents are served as MCP resources.

doc.description: a document id from the index or a search result (omit for the brief and the index)

full.description: true returns a large document whole instead of its outline

section.description: one section id or a list of section ids from the outline or a search result

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Send Ferrite a bug report, a suggestion, or feedback from your user. Omit secrets and private logs. Reuse the same request_id when retrying.

report.description: Full feedback, up to 8192 UTF-8 bytes.

request_id.description: A fresh UUID for this report; keep it for retries.

topic.description: Optional short subject, up to 240 UTF-8 bytes.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: SEARCH the Ferrite documentation: the published developer docs (the ferrite CLI and its local loop, `ferrite add` packages, authentication, Alloy, Rsx, data, agents, deploy, observe, limits), the support guides, and the platform documents `read_docs` serves. Large documents are searched section by section. Returns up to `limit` ranked matches {doc,title,section,heading,snippet,bytes,read}; read a match with read_docs and its `read` object. Every word of the query must appear in a match.

query.description: words to find, e.g. "sign-in allow list" or "ferrite dev egress"

tools.name: list_packages
tools.description: A one-page app (poll, form, sign-up sheet) needs no package. LIST the Ferrite source packages this server can compile into your app: vendored Rust source (sign-in, the Alloy runtime, crypto, cookies, MCP and ACP, the agent SDK, a browser engine and more), because a deployable app may depend on no crate but ferrite-app. Each entry is {name, version, root, summary, dependencies, files, bytes}; `query` keeps the packages whose name, summary or guide holds every word. read_package gives one package's guide, its files and the steps to use it; then `"packages": ["<name>"]` on code_gate and deploy_source adds its files for you. With a shell, `ferrite add <name>` writes the same files.

query.description: words to find, e.g. "sign-in" or "hmac"; omit for every package

tools.name: read_package
tools.description: A one-page app (poll, form, sign-up sheet) needs no package; alloy (thousands of lines) is for larger sites, auth for sign-in. READ one Ferrite source package. Without `file`: its version, module root, dependency closure in install order, its files (paths as they land in your app), its guide (README and setup), and `use`, the exact steps to compile it in: the crate-root lines for src/lib.rs, the `packages` argument for code_gate and deploy_source, and any Cargo features or spec entries it needs. With `file` (a path from that list, or README.md): that file's text as it lands in your app; a large file comes in parts, continued with `offset`.

file.description: a path from the package's file list (e.g. src/crypto/mod.rs), or README.md

name.description: a package name from list_packages, optionally name@version

offset.description: with `file`: the byte offset to continue from (the previous reply's next_offset)

tools.name: app_host
tools.description: The HOST an app has, or will have once deployed: `<shortcode>.<app domain>`, the shortcode derived from the app id `<account>/<app>` the way the platform names hosts, so an app's origin and OAuth callbacks are known before its first deploy (the `auth` package's secrets need them). Answers {app, host, origin, derived, callback_urls}; callback_urls are the auth package's GitHub and Google callbacks under its default /auth prefix. `app` is your app's name (the account comes from your bearer) or a full '<account>/<app>' id. After a deploy, build_status and list_apps report the host the platform assigned; where they differ, theirs is right.

app.description: the app's name as in your spec, or '<account>/<app>'

token.description: fallback bearer for clients that cannot send an Authorization header; when a header is present omit this argument, because a different token is refused

tools.name: provision
tools.description: Provision a DURABLE tenant account (open — no auth). Returns {Provisioned:{id,token}} (the bearer token) or {AlreadyProvisioned}. credit_micros is granted only where the platform's test credit mint is on; elsewhere a nonzero credit_micros is refused ({Rejected}, TEST_CREDIT_MINT_DISABLED) and nothing is created. Use the token on every other Ring 2 call (Authorization header preferred, or the 'token' argument).

tools.name: provision_ephemeral
tools.description: Open a trial account with free credit, ready to deploy at once, for a client that has no sign-in of its own: a script, or an agent without a browser. A connected application never needs it: it is already signed in to the person's account or to its own trial. Returns {EphemeralProvisioned:{account,token,claim_token,expires_at_ms,credit_micros}}: keep both tokens private.

tools.name: claim
tools.description: Claim an ephemeral session to a DURABLE owner, ending its subsidy. With owner_id: into that NEW account, created now (credit_micros is granted only where the platform's test credit mint is on); an id that already exists is refused. Without owner_id: into the EXISTING account your token authenticates (Authorization header or token), which that token authorizes. Needs claim_token from provision_ephemeral. Returns {Claimed:{account,token}} for a new account, {ClaimedInto:{account}} for your own.

token.description: fallback bearer for clients that cannot send an Authorization header; when a header is present omit this argument, because a different token is refused

tools.name: fund
tools.description: Grant TEST/development credit directly to the authenticated account; returns {Funded:{balance_micros}}. Admitted only where the platform's test credit mint is on (the front's `[commerce] test_credit_mint`); elsewhere it answers Rejected (TEST_CREDIT_MINT_DISABLED), grants nothing, and names the account's top-up page -- credit is bought there, through `billing_portal`. This is NOT a card payment: real human top-ups use `billing_portal`, then Stripe's hosted checkout. F-17 remains the precondition before credit denominates real money.

tools.name: build_status
tools.description: Read a build, test run or fork by build_id. Pass wait_s: 50 and it waits up to 50 s for the state to change before answering, so you need no sleep between calls; call it again until terminal (deploy build 4-8 min, test run 2-4, fork seconds). Do not end your turn or rely on a background timer meanwhile: in a non-interactive session that ends the session mid-build. deployed: live at https://<host>; give the user that URL (a new host can answer 504 for a minute or two while it is placed). rejected: `reasons` name each violation; fix before a new submission, preserving the selected source or committed-reference workflow. States: building, deploying (keep polling), deployed, undoing, rejected, failed (undone and refunded), stuck (an operator is paged; do not resubmit), tested / test_failed (test_ref). Never resubmit while building, deploying or undoing: that starts a second operation.

token.description: fallback bearer for clients that cannot send an Authorization header; when a header is present omit this argument, because a different token is refused

wait_s.description: Seconds (0-50) to wait for the state to change before answering; 0 answers at once.

tools.name: cancel_deploy
tools.description: End a deploy or fork that is still under way, by the build_id it returned: use it when a deploy is waiting on capacity and you want the name back. Returns {{BuildState:{{...}}}}. state 'cancelled' means nothing of it landed, any fee it took is returned, your running application is untouched and you can deploy again; 'deployed' means its operation had already finished, so the version is registered and `status` says whether it has landed, and this ends no trial; 'undoing' means it cannot land and is still being cleaned up. A wait has no time limit of its own, so this is how you end one.

tools.name: dead_letters
tools.description: List a queue service's dead letters, oldest first: messages delivered as many times as the queue allows without being acknowledged, which no consumer can take and which keep their bytes against the service's volume_mib until removed. Each says its id, its attempts and its size, and for an ordered message its key, its number and whether it killed its key. `total` is the queue's whole count; page with `after`, the last id seen.

tools.name: remove_dead_letters
tools.description: Remove a queue service's dead letters: `ids`, or `all`, one of the two. The bytes come back at once, so a queue refused for its volume_mib takes writes again. An id not dead now is passed over and not counted, so a live message is never removed. Removing the message an ordered key died on BRINGS THE KEY BACK: its later messages resume in order, with a gap where the removed number was, and `came_back` says how many per key; it can be none, since messages delivered together spend their attempts together. `all` takes up to 16000 in one call: call it again while `remaining` is above 0.

tools.name: fork
tools.description:
Copy a running app WITH its data (copy-on-write, seconds): {app, fork_app}, fork_app a new name such as <app>-karaoke. Returns {BuildStarted:{build_id}}; build_status reports deployed within seconds with the fork's host and one line per service (forked = copied). The original keeps serving, unchanged.
To change the copy: deploy_source ONCE with your edited files and the same spec except application name = fork_app exactly (artifact_key apps/<fork_app>@v1); keep the service names so the copied data stays. One build. Not rcs_checkout/rcs_commit/test_ref/deploy_ref: deploy_ref needs a manifest naming the fork and, when the platform requires tests, a passing commit-bound test verdict before deployment. Then give the user both URLs.
A fork refused with "is FULL" is a temporary capacity limit and costs nothing: retry the same fork call (each retry is free). Never substitute a fresh app: it would lose the data the user asked to keep.
as_of_unix_micros (optional) forks the state as of a past instant within 14 days. A code branch without data: rcs_branch. Details (not needed for the steps above): read_docs doc=forking.

token.description: fallback bearer for clients that cannot send an Authorization header; when a header is present omit this argument, because a different token is refused

tools.name: rcs_commit
tools.description: For an existing-app repair, send only changed files with complete contents; omitted files remain in the hosted repository, so do not re-upload unchanged generated packages. Save RcsCommitted.commit and use that exact reference for required test_ref and deploy_ref. Preserve the existing manifest and app identity. COMMIT files to the app's hosted source repository — INCREMENTAL: each commit overlays the previous tree, so you build the app up over MANY commits (many generations) instead of one giant upload; the FIRST commit claims the app. Optionally commit on a 'branch' (the branching model — a concurrent line on the SAME codebase; default 'main'). 'files' maps relative path -> file content. Returns {RcsCommitted:{app,branch,commit}}. `packages` names Ferrite source packages (list_packages, read_package) whose files the server adds to `files` under src/<root>/, with their dependencies', exactly as `ferrite add` writes them.

packages.description: Ferrite source packages to compile in, by name from list_packages ("name" or "name@version"). Do not send those files yourself: a changed copy is refused.

tools.name: deploy_ref
tools.description: For existing-app repairs, use the exact commit returned by rcs_commit; unchanged files are already in the repository. Deploys a revision committed with rcs_commit; not for a first deploy or a fork redeploy (deploy_source: one build, no verdict). When the platform requires tests, it refuses a commit without a passing test_ref verdict; the repository's ferrite.json must name exactly this app (for a fork, the fork's name). Deploy a COMMITTED revision of the app's repository: the platform checks out the source at the ref (omit for the 'main' head), reads the deployment spec FROM the repo ('spec_path', default 'ferrite.json'), attest-builds, and deploys — the version-controlled deploy flow (no monolithic single-call upload). ASYNCHRONOUS, for the same reason as deploy_source: it compiles your source, which takes minutes. Returns {BuildStarted:{build_id,app}}; then `build_status` (wait_s: 50). Do NOT resubmit while it is building.

token.description: fallback bearer for clients that cannot send an Authorization header; when a header is present omit this argument, because a different token is refused

tools.name: test_ref
tools.description: Runs a committed revision's #[test]s as its own 2-4 minute build. Run required tests against the exact committed revision before deploying it. TEST a COMMITTED revision (the platform's in-house test gate — no external CI): the platform checks out the app's repo at the ref (omit for the 'main' head), GATES + RUNS its tests (constrained test code against the platform's vetted test SDK), and stores a commit-bound verdict. When the platform requires tests, deploy_ref requires a passing verdict for that commit. ASYNCHRONOUS, and the longest of the three: it compiles the app AND its tests, then runs them. Returns {BuildStarted:{build_id,app}}; then `build_status` (wait_s: 50), which reports 'tested' (green) or 'test_failed' with the summary.

Returns {RcsCommitted:{app,branch,commit}}.

tools.name: rcs_land
tools.description: LAND a branch onto a protected trunk through the merge-result GATE (the trunk gate / branch protection): admitted ONLY if 'from' DESCENDS from the current 'into' tip (so the commit that was tested IS the commit that lands — the merge-queue insight; a stale branch behind the trunk is refused with status 'stale' — re-integrate via rcs_merge then re-test) AND, when the platform requires tests, 'from's tip carries a PASSING verdict (test_ref it first). A version-guarded fast-forward, so concurrent lands serialize. Returns {RcsLanded:{app,into,commit}}, or {RcsMerged:{status:'stale'|'conflict-retry'}}, or {Rejected} when the verdict gate fires.

tools.name: deploy_release
tools.description: Deploy a cut RELEASE to an ENVIRONMENT (env: prod | staging | canary | any [a-z0-9-]). 'prod' deploys the app's canonical id; another env deploys a derived '{app}-{env}' with its OWN subdomain, record, and instances (so staging and prod run side by side). The platform runs it AND advances the environment's audit log. It runs as a durable operation (the attested build, the deploy, then the environment's pointer as its LAST step), so a large application's gates never hold the call: it returns BuildStarted{build_id} at once; poll build_status -- `deployed` once the environment's pointer names the release (with the host and generation), `pointer_denied` if the environment's deploy authority refused the advance (the application still deployed). Do NOT resubmit while it is building.

Returns BuildStarted{build_id}; poll build_status as for deploy_release.

tools.name: preview_ref
tools.description: Deploy a COMMITTED revision as an UNGATED, throwaway PREVIEW on its OWN subdomain (a validation copy, safe by isolation: NOT test-gated, NEVER charged, NEVER a permanent name claim; authorized by owning the base app). Auto-expires (TTL) and is swept. Preview un-green code on purpose before you cut a release. ASYNCHRONOUS: it compiles your source, which takes minutes. Returns {BuildStarted:{build_id,app}}; poll `build_status`, which answers {PreviewDeployed:{app,preview_app,host,expires_at_ms,commit}} once it is live. Do NOT resubmit while it is building.

tools.name: delete_preview

Authorized by owning the base app (a foreign-namespace id is refused); idempotent (deleting an already-gone preview succeeds); the TTL sweep composes (a deleted preview is skipped). Returns {PreviewDeleted:{preview_app}}.

tools.name: estimate_cost
tools.description: PRE-DEPLOY COST + CAPS ESTIMATE (the try-before-you-buy surface — charges nothing, deploys nothing): validates the spec exactly as a deploy would and reports what a deploy WOULD charge now (the deploy fee), your balance + tier, the per-app instance count + per-instance compute bound that WILL apply (ephemeral tier: clamped to 1 instance and 256 MiB / 50% CPU per instance, enforced as a cgroup bound; durable tier: your spec's compute, or the platform default when undeclared), your tier's caps (source size, session TTL, subsidized credit), and honest notes on what is priced (the deploy fee; per-request serving where enabled) vs projected: the occupancy / stream-group / storage / request rates are the FLEET-DERIVED pricing model (each resource priced from its measured provider-cost driver; anchor: 1,000,000 micros = $1.00), returned as `rates`, with per-app `occupancy_micros_per_hour` + `projected_monthly_micros` projections and, in `notes`, which prices apply at this read and what each service's data costs by axis (occupancy is metered hourly against your balance: reserved compute and data; an exhausted balance suspends your apps; `service_costs` reads the same figures for what is deployed). Call it BEFORE deploy_source / deploy_ref to see your footprint — and how 'claim' lifts the ephemeral caps (credit beyond the subsidy is bought through 'billing_portal'). Returns {Estimate:{tier,balance_micros,deploy_fee_micros,spec_valid,violations,apps,caps,notes,rates}}.

Owner-gated; the value is write-only (never returned by the API). Bounds: name [A-Za-z0-9_.-] <=64, value <=64 KiB, <=64 secrets per app. Returns {SecretSet:{app,name}}.

tools.name: retry_park
tools.description: Retry a PARKED app: one whose instances crash-looped, so its rollout was paused and further deploys answer ParkedMutationRefused. Fix the cause first, then call this: the app is re-admitted against your account's current balance and quotas and its rollout resumes. tools.name: notifications
tools.description: Read your NOTIFICATION FEED — the platform's durable, account-scoped 'your production changed state' events: a payment credited, your apps SUSPENDED because occupancy charges exhausted the balance, a deploy REFUSED for insufficient funds. This is how you find out something happened to your production that you did not initiate. Check it when something seems off, after funding, and periodically while you run production. Oldest first; 'limit' returns the newest N (default 50; 0 = all retained). Returns {Notifications:{account,lines:[{at_ms,severity,kind,body,dedup,source}]}}.

tools.name: set_notify_channel
tools.description: PUSH: register a signed-webhook RECEIVER for your notification feed, so the platform TELLS you when your production changes state instead of you polling. `url` must be https. The platform returns a shared `secret_hex` ONCE (it is sealed at rest afterwards): every delivery POSTs {"signature":"t=<unix>,v1=<hmac-sha256>","payload":"<the event JSON, verbatim>"}, where the HMAC is over "{t}.{payload}" with that secret — the SAME scheme Stripe uses (and that this platform verifies on inbound provider webhooks), so verify it with any standard implementation. Deliveries are at-least-once and resume EXACTLY where they stopped: the cursor advances only on a 2xx, retries back off (5s..5min), and nothing is ever lost — the durable feed (`notifications`) remains the source of truth. Setting a channel starts from NOW (no backlog replay). Delivery rides the platform's audited egress gate under a token scoped to YOUR url alone. Returns {NotifyChannelSet:{url,secret_hex}}.

secret_hex.description: optional: your own signing secret (16..=64 bytes of hex); omit to have the platform generate one

tools.description: Prepare a ROTATION of your bearer token: answers a NEW token that works only after you confirm it with confirm_token (within 15 minutes); your current token keeps working until then. It becomes live and the token it replaces stops working. Safe to repeat.

tools.name: resume
tools.description: RESUME a PARKED application: the platform parks an app that crash-loops or whose account ran out of credit (`status` shows `park_phase` and `park_retry_after_ms`). This retries it now through fresh account admission instead of waiting for the automatic retry. Answers {ParkRetryStarted:{app,generation}} when the app is placed again (follow it with `status`), {ParkRetryBlocked:{app,resource,requested,cap,retry_after_ms}} when admission still refuses it (add credit through `billing_portal` or lower its compute, then retry), {ParkedMutationRefused:{app,phase,retry_after_ms}} while a retry is already pending, or an Error when the app is not parked. The Dashboard's Resume button is this call.
